searchText: Try the panda magic that <@84562395988508672> cooked. I used that voodoo to read ethrex logs from before a reboot forky probably needs some love, not sure if we have it right now Couldn't find anything about voodoo. Would there be any links to this please? ethpandaops/panda I could try, but if possible I'd be just as happy to access whatever datastore might hold these, copy the logs, etc, and go from there. So far I've kept my LLM access set up with 0 credentials to anything in its own isolated space, so its blast radius is... well, I guess, the Internet. But nothing private I've looked for old Docker logs before and I have no idea if they're even preserved panda spins up a sandbox container to do anything, so your blast radius is kinda just the sandbox container. it can't access the host to do anything. it uses github oauth the to authenticate against the datasources. https://ethpandaops.io/posts/panda/ (sandbox section of the post tells you what permissions the sandbox is configured with) You can also use panda as a standalone cli and use it to just return logs for you, but its gonna be a clunkier way to use it. but if you want to avoid the cli altogether, you can - the logs are visible in grafana and or via ssh + docker logs 😄 Just ask the LLM for the right panda CLI commands and run them yourself 🙂 well, at any given time the docker logs cover 10-20 minutes as far as I can tell unless there are more elsewhere that `docker logs` doesn't show. I already use that that doesnt sound right, docker logs should have a much longer timeframe - its usually limimted by the size it takes up on the host and we used to set it at like 500mb or something relatively high. if not, they will be visible in grafana under the explore tab, choose clickhouse logs as the option ``` devops@nimbus-nethermind-1 ➜ ~ date && docker logs beacon | head -n1 Sat Jun 6 09:54:03 AM UTC 2026 WRN 2026-06-06 09:01:47.468+00:00 Unknown constants in config file unknowns="[EIP7928_FORK_VERSION, MAX_REQUEST_PAYLOADS, MAX_REQUEST_INCLUSION_LIST, EIP7928_FORK_EPOCH, INCLUSION_LIST_DUE_BPS, MAX_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST]" devops@nimbus-nethermind-1 ➜ ~ docker logs beacon | wc 306389 4861067 65274070 ``` the amount of logs is pretty high 😅 ``` panda clickhouse query clickhouse-raw "SELECT Timestamp, SeverityText, Body FROM external.otel_logs WHERE ServiceName='beacon' AND ResourceAttributes['network']='glamsterdam-devnet-5' AND ResourceAttributes['host.name']='nimbus-erigon-1' AND Timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR ORDER BY Timestamp DESC LIMIT 100" ``` <@654267572107083777> you can switch out host.name `nimbus-erigon-1` with `nimbus-nethermind-1` and you should be able to get any interval of logs ah, ok, from Svalbard I'd misunderstood how panda was described, it's more than a pure LLM tool Its a access layer to our tooling for your terminal 🙂 Yeah, looks useful indeed only 21.9M logs to go through 😉 I mean, arguably a better problem to have at least than 0 logs. But yeah, too much data is its own challenge

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
panda spins up a sandbox container to do anything, so your blast radius is kinda just the sandbox container. it can't access the host to do anything. it uses github oauth the to authenticate against the datasources. https://ethpandaops.io/posts/panda/ (sandbox section of the post tells you what permissions the sandbox is configured with)

You can also use panda as a standalone cli and use it to just return logs for you, but its gonna be a clunkier way to use it. 

but if you want to avoid the cli altogether, you can - the logs are visible in grafana and or via ssh + docker logs  😄

excerpts.author: qu0b
excerpts.content: Just ask the LLM for the right panda CLI commands and run them yourself 🙂

that doesnt sound right, docker logs should have a much longer timeframe - its usually limimted by the size it takes up on the host and we used to set it at like 500mb or something relatively high.

if not, they will be visible in grafana under the explore tab, choose clickhouse logs as the option
